sentences.text: Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is repeat fourth application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the applicant/accused, relating to FIR/Crime No.588/2022 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station- Tejaji Nagar, District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable u/S 420, 467,
468 and 471 of IPC.
2 .

Her first and second bail applications were dismissed as withdrawn vide orders dated 05.07.2023 passed by this Court in MCRC No.19950/2023 and 25.10.2023 passed by this Court in MCRC No.47013/2023 respectively and thereafter third bail application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 07.03.2024 passed MCRC No.55314/2024.

sentences.text: Prosecution story, in brief is that during 24.10.2021 to 12.09.2022, applicant/accused introduced herself as SDM, Indore, assured the complainant Nitin Patil to provide a job in a government department and had taken Rs.11,00,000/- from the complainant.
Applicant had also taken the educational documents and ID card of the complainant and thereafter, she issued forged appointment and joining letter.
Later on, the complainant found that the applicant does not hold any government post and she had cheated the complainant and had also committed forgery.
4 . Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and she has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that at the time of dismissal of earlier bail application of the applicant on merit, statement of Nitin Patil (P.W.-1) has not been considered properly.

It is submitted that in paragraph 3 of the examination-in-chief Nitin Patil (P.W.-1) has stated that applicant/accused called the complainant Nitin Patil at Collectorate on 12.09.2022 and he gave him appointment letter and I- Card, while the applicant was in custody since 08.09.2022 in another criminal case therefore, the question of applicant/accused meeting the complainant on 12.09.2022 does not arises.
It is submitted that trial court had not framed charges under section 419 of the I.P.C.
It is further submitted that questioned documents has not been sent to hand writing expert till date.

It is also submitted that however seizure witnesses Radheshyam (P.W.-6) and Satendra Patidar (P.W.-8) have supported the case of the prosecution but there are material contradictions in their statements therefore, their statement is not reliable.
Applicant is in custody since 17.09.2022.

Conclusion of trial will take considerable long time for its disposal,
therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

5 . On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and submits that questioned documents had been sent to a hand writing expert for examination but later on it has been received back with direction to send again along with specimen hand writing of the applicant.
In this respect further investigation is pending.
It is also submitted that after collecting specimen hand writing and signature it shall be send for examination.

It is further submitted that Nitin Patil (P.W.-1) and seizure witnesses Radheshyam (P.W.-6) and Satendra Patidar (P.W.-8) have fully supported the case of the prosecution and at this stage statement of the witnesses cannot be appreciated.
The offence is serious in nature.
After rejection of earlier bail applications of the applicant there is no change in circumstances, therefore this repeat bail application of the applicant is liable to be rejected.

6. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that it is not a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, this repeat bail application is dismissed.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE ajit Neelam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98828973/
